newsitem.title: INDIA: India blaze kills at least 120 Hindu devotees.
newsitem.headline: India blaze kills at least 120 Hindu devotees.

text.p: A raging fire fanned by gusting winds tore through bamboo and straw shelters at a Hindu convention in eastern India on Sunday, killing at least 120 devotees and injuring 165, police said.
"We have recovered 120 bodies so far," Santosh Upadhyay, police chief of Baripada town in Orissa state, said.
"The death toll could be even higher as there is still a heap of charred bodies inside the makeshift arrangement for the devotees."
Authorities said some 15,000 people were attending the conference in Baripada town when the blaze swept through eight thatched huts erected for the event on a football ground.
The home (interior) secretary of Orissa state, S.C. Hota, said strong winds fanned the fire, which broke out at about 3:30 p.m. (1000 GMT).
The blaze swiftly engulfed eight makeshift huts in the camp at Baripada, 175 km (110 miles) southwest of Calcutta, he said.
Local news agencies said unofficial reports put the death toll at more than 250 people. "We will be able to tell the death toll only tomorrow when we clear the debris," Upadhyay said.
The fire was believed to have been caused by either a short circuit or a gas cylinder that exploded, Hota said. Many of the bodies were charred beyond recognition.
"It was a ghastly scene," Amarlal Bose, a resident of Baripada, told Reuters in New Delhi by telephone.

"People with serious burn injuries were being carried off in ambulances. It was a chaotic situation, with people running helter skelter to know the fate of the delegates. Bodies were lying here and there."
Most of the victims were men napping after lunch at the annual national convention, dedicated to the memory of the Hindu guru Nigamananda, Hota said.
"The number of exits at the camp was very limited," Hota said, noting that the shelters were made out of bamboo and straw. "That was a problem."
Two fire tenders at the camp were pressed into service but were unable to contain the raging flames, he said. The state government ordered an administrative inquiry into the fire.

"The makeshift houses were completely burned down, reduced to ashes," Bose said, adding that straw had been spread on the ground to serve as bedding. The temperature in the region was 32 degrees Celsius (90 Fahrenheit) and the weather was dry.

Women and children attending the convention which began last Thursday were in 10 huts in a separate area of the camp, authorities said. Residents said the convention's concluding ceremony had been set for later on Sunday.
"The only good thing was that the females' camp was not affected by the fire," Bose said.
A total of 165 injured were taken to the district hospital, Hota said.
Forty-three doctors were attending to the injured, and a medical team with special equipment was driving from Cuttack city, 175 km (110 miles) to the south, Hota said.
PTI quoted Orissa chief minister J.B. Patnaik as saying he had ordered the payment of 25,000 rupees ($700) to the victims' families and 10,000 ($280) to the seriously injured.

It was believed to be the deadliest fire in India since about 425 people, mostly children, died when a blaze ripped through a school prize-giving ceremony in the northern town of Dabwali in December 1995.
